clue.text: How unfair to be none too bright!

definitions.meaning: the exclamation for an outrageous imposition, as in protesting that a demand is too much
slow-witted or rather stupid, a colloquial way of calling someone dim

explanation.surface: A remark that it is unjust to be lacking in intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British idioms: an imposition is called 'a bit thick' when excessive, and a dull person is called 'a bit thick' for being dim.

clue.text: Ben gets a little sweet in the interim?

indicators.note: Ben gets, or takes in, the other piece, so the letters of Ben hold it inside

parts.note: twee means cutesy and a little too sweet

explanation.surface: Ben has a small snack between meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' signals the container: Ben takes something in. The question mark admits the definition is adverbial, as in 'in between' times.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanwhile, during the intervening time, is what the adverb means.

clue.text: Taste butter? That's a puzzle!

parts.note: a tang is a sharp flavour or taste
something that butts, as a male sheep does with its horns

explanation.surface: A dairy food tasting session ends up baffling someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the spread: read it as 'one who butts', the ram. A tangram is a Chinese puzzle of seven pieces forming shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangram is a dissection puzzle in which seven flat shapes are arranged into a given figure.

clue.text: Really snug in divine location

indicators.note: the snug place sits in the middle of the word for divine

parts.note: holy means sacred or divine
a nest is a snug, cosy retreat

explanation.surface: A cosy spot tucked away in some sacred place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snug' looks like an adjective but stands for a noun, a cosy retreat. 'Really' is the definition as an interjection of disbelief or emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are interjections of exasperation or emphasis meaning truly, as in 'Honestly, what next?'

clue.text: Fortune offered to see Kelvin is paid off

parts.note: K is the symbol for the kelvin, the unit of temperature
a bill or debt that is paid off is met

explanation.surface: Someone is told their luck has turned once Kelvin has cleared his debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is fate or destiny, the lot that fortune hands out.

clue.text: Does my pun get republished under another name?

indicators.note: printing the words afresh rearranges them, so their letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: An author wonders whether a reissued joke should come out under a pen name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get republished' rearranges DOES MY PUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseudonym is an alias or pen name used in place of a real one.

clue.text: Those overseeing ops rooms!

parts.note: military operations, the business of war
dens are small private rooms

explanation.surface: An exclamation about the officers who run operations rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'ops rooms' as war dens, but the whole is the people in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Wardens are guardians or supervisors who keep watch over a place or people.

clue.text: My clanger upset his flock

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the words are thrown about

explanation.surface: A vicar admits a blunder of his offended the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges MY CLANGER; the whole clue describes the minister, whose flock is his congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of the church is the shepherd of a congregation, traditionally called his flock.

clue.text: Fix everything after this month

indicators.note: after places the word for everything behind the abbreviation

parts.note: inst., short for instant, is the old letter-writing term for this month
all means everything

explanation.surface: Arrange everything to be sorted once this month is over.
explanation.walkthrough: INST. (instant) dates a letter to the current month, an old commercial convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To install is to set up or fit equipment in place.

clue.text: Removing the pits from fruit caused Stephen's death

definitions.meaning: taking the stones out of cherries or plums
Saint Stephen, the first Christian martyr, was killed by having rocks thrown at him

explanation.surface: A grim joke that coring fruit somehow killed a man named Stephen.
explanation.walkthrough: In Acts, Stephen was the first martyr, put to death by being pelted with rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoning means both de-pitting fruit and execution by pelting with rocks.

clue.text: Grumble when American goes back below

indicators.note: going back means the abbreviation is read from right to left

parts.note: under means below

explanation.surface: Someone moans as the American retreats to the lower deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Maunder is a dialect and literary verb for mutter or complain, as well as ramble.

clue.text: Others are awfully distressed

indicators.note: awfully suggests the words are badly done, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Other people are terribly upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges OTHERS ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartsore is a literary adjective for grief-stricken or deeply pained.

clue.text: Was furious about Virginia being sacked

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for being furious encloses the state's code

parts.note: raged means was furious
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Someone flew into a rage over Virginia losing her job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' is the plundering sense, as of a captured city, not losing a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacked city has been looted and laid waste, which is what ravaged means.

clue.text: Lawyer gains entry to a new milieu

indicators.note: putting the letters in new surroundings rearranges them

explanation.surface: A solicitor gets into a fresh social setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new milieu' rearranges ENTRY TO A.
explanation.definitionFit: An attorney is a legal practitioner, chiefly in the US.

clue.text: Brutish parent dressed in blue

indicators.note: dressed in means clothed in, so the dye word wraps round the parent

parts.note: anil is the indigo plant and its blue dye
ma is a mother, a parent

explanation.surface: A rough mother wearing blue clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed in' signals the container. 'blue' is not a colour word in the usual sense but anil, a dye from the indigo plant.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means beastly, coarse and physical, like a beast.

clue.text: Exercise machine

definitions.meaning: the old sense of the act of applying or putting into use, as in the exercise of power
a device or piece of equipment for a household task

explanation.surface: A gym apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is dated: an appliance once meant an application or employment of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a device and, archaically, the application or use of something.

clue.text: Energy-booster needed to write article about Ireland's partition

indicators.note: about places the article round the other letters

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: partition means dividing up, so the letters of the word are broken apart and rearranged

parts.note: the word Ireland, whose possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A stimulant is required to write a piece on the division of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partition' rearranges IRELAND into DRENALI, and 'about' wraps the article round it. 'needed to write' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenalin is the hormone released in stress that gives a surge of energy.

clue.text: Powerful family makes yard turn unpleasant

indicators.note: turn means the abbreviation is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: nasty means unpleasant

explanation.surface: A ruling clan makes their garden unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a line of rulers or an influential family across generations.

clue.text: Bird and rodent pursuing Titus

annotationWithheld.why: Bird and rodent pursuing Titus (8): TIT + MOUSE, but 'Titus' gives TIT with no indicator and 'Bird' is needed both as definition and as TIT; no honest parse

clue.text: Tortuous obstacle beset relations

indicators.note: beset means surrounded, so the word for an obstacle encloses the relations

parts.note: a snag is an obstacle or hitch
kin are relations

explanation.surface: A winding hurdle that caused family problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beset' signals the container: the obstacle surrounds the relations.
explanation.definitionFit: Snaking means winding and twisting, like a serpent's path.

clue.text: Challenge one heartless man confining a dog

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: confining means holding inside, so the outer letters enclose the dog
heartless means losing the middle, so only the first and last letters remain

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: A man with no heart hems in a dog and gets challenged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle of 'man', and 'confining' puts the dog between the remaining letters; 'a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn a claim is to dispute or call it into question.

clue.text: Strong-smelling dope hidden in boat

indicators.note: the information is tucked inside the boat, so it goes within that word

parts.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed boat
gen is slang for information, also called dope

explanation.surface: Drugs are smuggled aboard a vessel that reeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' is not drugs but information; 'hidden in' here means put inside the boat word, not a run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent means sharp and powerful to the nose.

clue.text: Resents Barnaby gaining place in grammar school

indicators.note: getting a place at the school means going inside its abbreviation

parts.note: Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: Someone is bitter that Barnaby won a grammar school place.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnaby Rudge is a Charles Dickens novel; a grammar school is a selective British state secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: Grudges as a verb means begrudges or feels aggrieved about.

clue.text: Tell stories about stylish German undies

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the lying word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: to tell stories is to lie
in means fashionable or stylish

explanation.surface: Someone fibs about fashionable German underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container: the fibbing word goes round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear, colloquially undies.

clue.text: Eat after ten and you'll need antiseptic

indicators.note: after puts the eating word behind the figures for ten

parts.note: IO looks like the figures 10
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Dinner after ten o'clock will need a disinfectant.
explanation.walkthrough: IO for ten is a crossword visual pun: the letters I and O resemble the digits 1 and 0.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodine in solution is used to disinfect cuts and wounds.

clue.text: Eccentric at large without a partner

definitions.meaning: an oddball or misfit who does not fit with the rest
the one left over when everyone else pairs up

explanation.surface: An oddball on the loose with no companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at large' adds to the picture of a loner; the phrase is both the misfit and the unpaired one left over.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a misfit who differs from the group, and the single person left when others form pairs.

clue.text: Seven days in a hospital room proves difficult

indicators.note: in puts the week abbreviation inside the hospital phrase

parts.note: a ward is a room in a hospital
WK is short for week, seven days

explanation.surface: A week's stay on a ward turns out to be hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container: the week goes inside 'a ward'. 'proves' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward means hard to handle or troublesome.

clue.text: Inn serves vegetable one pole discarded

indicators.note: discarded means thrown away, so those letters are dropped from the vegetable

parts.note: the aubergine, called eggplant in the US
I is the Roman numeral for one
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A pub serves aubergine, minus one pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discarded' removes I and N from AUBERGINE.
explanation.definitionFit: An auberge is a French inn or country hotel.

clue.text: Study traffic guide to make deliveries

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a road sign guides traffic

explanation.surface: Learn the road signs before driving a delivery van.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign goods is to send or hand them over for delivery.

clue.text: One-time priest displayed energy and skill

parts.note: ex means former or one-time

indicators.note: displayed suggests the letters are spread out and set out anew in a different order

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A former clergyman showed vigour and ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' rearranges PRIEST into PERTIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise is special skill or know-how.
